confidence_reason: The round-2 agents already converge (ladder medians $73-77). My corrections (filings-based P/E median ~16.6x, fair value pulled to the scenario means, agent_5's FCF leg) mainly lower fair values, which the ladders never fully reflected. So they justify only a small trim of the upper tail (bull cases assumed re-rating to a 19.6x 'median' that is really ~16.6x). None of this settles a disagreement large enough to replace the mean. Round 3 raises it to medium: the AV review settled, from verified price and multiple history, that a 12-month narrative de-rating with EPS intact has just happened (forward P/E -45% while implied forward EPS +28%, LYFT -55%). That is a gap every agent left open, and it moves the ladder median about $4. It is not high because the scenario's 15% weight and 13.3x multiple are estimates, and the forward-P/E history is an aggregator series whose basis cannot be reproduced. The fair value and sizing.confidence changes still flow through to rubric.py.
thesis_break_reason: Agents give $52-54 (mean $52.6), and I keep it. That is ~11x haircut Oct-2027 NTM EPS (~$4.8) and ~7x NTM EV/EBITDA ($52.6 x 2.02B + $7.33B net debt - $8.76B investments = $104.8B over $15.0B), Lyft-like (6.3x). Trading there would mean estimate cuts, not volatility: bookings growth toward ~10%, AV operators visibly taking US share before their 2028 dates, a sized AV program well above $10B or fleet ownership on the balance sheet, or DH financing pushing gross leverage above 2x. It is also ~26% below the CEO's $70.96 open-market buy. Round 3: kept. A narrative-only de-rating with EPS on the $4.80 path lands at ~$59-64 (12.27x-13.32x), above $52.6, so it should not trigger the break. Reaching $52.6 needs ~11x on intact EPS, a -34% compression from today's 16.71x (10.96/16.71, derived): three of the five 12-month compressions since Sep-2024 (-14% to -29%) stay above it; only the latest two (-39.7% from 32.25x and -44.9% from 30.89x) went further. Or it needs estimate cuts, which is the thesis failing. Lyft-like 7.89x on $4.80 ($37.9) means share loss, not narrative.

The Q3 guide implies +28-35% EPS growth; consensus Oct-2027 NTM EPS is ~$5.3-5.5 (MarketScreener table last updated Feb 2026; stockanalysis FY27 $4.43 is ~2.5% below it) and agents haircut it ~10-14% to ~$4.7-5.0 for AV and DH drag.

fair_value.reason: I rebuilt the blend with the multiples the agents' own base cases use. P/E: 16.5x on ~$4.80 Oct-2027 NTM EPS (consensus ~$5.3-5.5 less ~10-12%) = $79.2, weight 45%; 16.5x is about UBER's own NTM multiple today (16.7x) and, after the citation gate's filings-based rebuild of the peer table, also about the all-peer median (16.6x), so no further AV discount is taken beyond the EPS haircut. EV/EBITDA: 9.2x filings-based NTM peer median on ~$15.0B NTM adj. EBITDA = EV $138.0B, less $7.33B net debt ex-leases ($12.72B debt - $5.39B cash and ST investments, Q2 8-K), plus $8.76B of non-DH investments at carrying value (10-Q), / ~2.02B shares at the horizon = $69.0, weight 25%. FCF: post-SBC NTM FCF ~$11B at today's 7.33% forward post-SBC yield ($12.43B forward FCF, 0.25 x FY26E $10.49B + 0.75 x FY27E $13.08B MarketScreener, less the $2.03B midpoint of the 2026 SBC guide, over a $141.9B market cap = $69.48 x 2.043B) = $150.0B / 2.02B = $74.3, weight 30%. The blend is $75.2, in line with the agents' scenario means ($74.5-77.0) and ~8% above the $69.48 Oct-5 close. Round 3 (AV narrative scenario): the blend above is the no-de-rating value. In the narrative scenario, every leg moves to a de-rated multiple on unchanged fundamentals: P/E 13.32x (core-7 median) x $4.80 = $63.94; EV/EBITDA 7.93x (core-7 median) x $15.0B = $118.95B - $7.33B + $8.76B = $120.38B / 2.02B = $59.59; FCF yield 7.33% x 16.71/13.32 = 9.20%, $11.0B / 9.20% = $119.6B / 2.02B = $59.22; 0.45/0.25/0.30 blend = $61.44. Probability-weighted (15% estimate): 0.85 x $75.2 + 0.15 x $61.44 = $73.14, so $73.1 (estimate). That is ~5.3% above the $69.48 Oct-5 close and in line with the round-3 ladder's mixture mean of ~$73.4.

what_exists: A long, sector-wide de-rating while fundamentals grew. In every 12-month window since Sep-2024 (5 overlapping windows, about 2 independent years), UBER's forward P/E fell 14-45%. In the latest two (Jun-25 -> Jun-26 -39.7%, Sep-25 -> Oct-26 -44.9%), the stock fell 23-30% while implied forward EPS rose ~28% (stockanalysis ratios; derived). LYFT's forward P/E fell 37.5% and 54.7% over the same windows, so this is not only Uber-specific (DH, AV capex).
Waymo headlines are consistently negative for UBER on the day (-9.6%, -5.0%, -4.3%). The Dec-2024 one took ~2 months and a strong earnings print to recover.
what_does_not_exist: Evidence that Tesla ('Elon') narrative specifically is priced into UBER for long stretches. Tesla's events gave +10.8% (relief rally, fully reversed in 10 sessions), +1.7% and -3.5% (not reversed, but confounded), and results days average ±2%. The sticky narrative is Waymo's.
A clean split between AV narrative and Uber's own drivers in the 2025-26 de-rating. Each leg included an earnings-day drop on guide or AV-spend commentary, and the DH bid added leverage.

A sourced history of UBER's NTM P/E on the filings basis the comps use. The stockanalysis forward P/E series cannot be reproduced from its own estimates (citation gate), so it is used only for trend and size of compression.

Evidence that de-ratings never reverse: after the Sep-Dec 2024 compression (-26.6%) the price fully recovered by 2025-02-07 and the forward P/E regained ~40% of its drop by Jun-2025 (28.21 -> 32.25 vs 38.43, derived) as results came through.
evidence_summary.maturation_caveat: Part of the 38x -> 17x compression since 2024 is normal multiple decay as EPS growth slowed from >50% to ~28% (estimate: implied forward EPS = price / forward P/E rose 75.16/38.43 = 1.96 -> 97.97/30.89 = 3.17, +62%, Sep-24 to Sep-25, and 3.17 -> 69.08/17.03 = 4.06, +28%, Sep-25 to Oct-26; aggregator basis). That is why the scenario uses -20% (to the core-7 median), not the observed -45%.

scenario.reasoning: For a higher weight: UBER's multiple fell in both independent recent years, by 20% and 45%, and LYFT's fell in step, so a flat 16.5x for 12 months (the base case at ~50%) is not the historical norm. The horizon (2027-10-05) falls three months before Waymo's own app in Uber's two exclusive Waymo cities, while Waymo prepares 20+ cities and Tesla builds Cybercab and adds metros, so the narrative will probably be at least as live at the horizon as it is now. For a lower weight: UBER already sits at the all-peer median (16.7x), not at 28-38x where the past 12-month compressions started (Sep-24 38.43, Dec-24 28.21, Mar-25 29.83, Jun-25 32.25, Sep-25 30.89). In the 2024 episode the price recovered within ~2 months (2025-02-07) and the forward P/E regained ~40% of its drop within ~6 months. A 13.3x multiple on $4.80 would mean a ~9% post-SBC FCF yield with ~50% of FCF going to buybacks. And agents 2 and 4 already put ~25% on narrative-heavy bears at 11-12x with only ~6% EPS trims, so the severe version of this risk was already in the distribution. 15% covers the missing middle state without double counting those bears. It comes pro rata from base and bull (weights about 0.506/0.246 -> 0.405/0.197), and the bear stays at 0.248. Sensitivity: 10% gives median $72.3, confidence 0.42, fair value $73.8; 20% gives $69.9, 0.37, $72.4.
